selection: Knowledge-base entries with status source-verified or evidence-derived and use class 1-3 (class 4 'not for automated evaluation' and excluded entries are left out).

entries.guidance: Malaysian labels must declare energy, protein, available carbohydrate (excluding fibre), total sugars, fat and sodium per 100 g/ml (or per pack if single portion) and per serving.
entries.nutripal_use: Defines which nutrients can be expected; carbohydrate on Malaysian labels already excludes fibre, so NutriPal must not subtract fibre again.
entries.caution: Imported US-style labels show 'Total carbohydrate' that includes fibre; keep the label's own definition.

entries.guidance: 2,000 mg sodium is equivalent to 5 g salt (about 1 level teaspoon).
entries.nutripal_use: Convert labels that print salt into sodium before any rule runs.
entries.caution: Teaspoon equivalents vary (1,794-1,959 mg in S01 App D/F); say 'about'.

entries.guidance: Low fat <=3 g/100 g or <=1.5 g/100 ml; low saturated fat <=1.5 g/100 g or <=0.75 g/100 ml and <=10% of the food's energy; low sugar <=5 g/100 g or <=2.5 g/100 ml; low sodium <=120 mg/100 g or <=60 mg/100 ml; very low sodium <=40 mg/100 g or <=20 mg/100 ml; low cholesterol <=20 mg/100 g or <=10 mg/100 ml.
entries.nutripal_use: Informational badge: 'meets Malaysia's low-sodium level'. These are claim conditions, not health ratings.
entries.caution: Never call a product 'healthy' because it meets a claim level.

entries.guidance: Source of fibre >=3 g/100 g or >=1.5 g/100 ml; high fibre >=6 g/100 g or >=3 g/100 ml.
entries.nutripal_use: Positive informational badge for fibre.

entries.guidance: Sodium-free <5 mg, very low <=35 mg, low <=140 mg per serving; reduced = 25% less; light = 50% less.
entries.nutripal_use: Explain US-labelled imports only; Malaysian claims use per 100 g/ml.
entries.caution: Do not apply to Malaysian claims.

entries.guidance: FSA per-100 g/ml low/medium/high thresholds for fat, saturated fat, sugars and salt; drinks use stricter values (half for fat, saturated fat and sugars; lower medium/high bounds for salt).
entries.nutripal_use: Product-level colour independent of the user.
entries.caution: Malaysia has no national traffic-light scheme: a named design decision.
entries.source: Carried over from 'NutriPal Nutrition Analysis Rules' (8 Nov 2026) 2023

entries.topic: Malaysian claims agree with FSA green
entries.guidance: Malaysian 'low' levels equal the FSA green upper limits for fat, saturated fat, sugars (food and drink) and sodium in foods; only sodium in drinks differs (Malaysia 60 mg/100 ml vs FSA 120 mg/100 ml).
entries.nutripal_use: Strengthens use of FSA green for Malaysian products.
entries.caution: Show the Malaysian drink sodium badge separately.

entries.guidance: An individual's calculated energy requirement has a large confidence interval; comparing intake with it does not show whether needs are met. Plan with the estimate, then monitor weight and adjust.
entries.nutripal_use: Why NutriPal calls energy targets estimates and labels energy shares as approximate.
entries.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2023

entries.guidance: Adult TEE = sex- and activity-specific equations in age (y), height (cm), weight (kg); e.g. women, low active: 575.77 - 7.01 age + 6.60 height + 12.14 weight. RMSE 339 kcal (men), 246 kcal (women).
entries.nutripal_use: Optional replacement for Mifflin-St Jeor x activity factor.
entries.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2023

entries.guidance: Inactive 1.0<=PAL<1.53; low active 1.53-<1.68; active 1.68-<1.85; very active 1.85-<2.50.
entries.nutripal_use: Maps NutriPal's activity question to an equation.
entries.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2023

entries.guidance: Energy metabolism data are sparse for diverse racial and ethnic groups.
entries.nutripal_use: Limitation statement for the report and chatbot.
entries.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2023

entries.guidance: Current emphasis is on healthy dietary patterns rather than individual nutrient composition.
entries.nutripal_use: Why NutriPal does not give a single 'healthy/unhealthy' verdict.
entries.source: Ministry of Health Malaysia / Academy of Medicine Malaysia 2023

entries.guidance: Choose minimally processed foods; plant-based meat alternatives may be ultra-processed with added sugar, saturated fat and salt.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education only: processing level is not on the nutrition table.
entries.source: Ministry of Health Malaysia / Academy of Medicine Malaysia 2023

entries.guidance: Water should be the primary beverage; replace sugar-sweetened beverages (including juices) with water or low/no-calorie drinks.
entries.applies_to: Adults with or at risk of diabetes
entries.nutripal_use: Supports a drink-specific sugar insight.

entries.guidance: A 'less'/'more' (comparative) claim needs the two foods to differ by at least 25% (10% for micronutrients), and the absolute difference must be at least the amount needed for a 'low' or 'source' claim. Energy 'low' is 40 kcal/100 g or 20 kcal/100 ml.
entries.nutripal_use: Used as NutriPal's test for a meaningful difference in product comparisons (tab 5).

entries.guidance: Eight adult EER equations (age 19+, by sex and four activity categories) in age (y), height (cm) and weight (kg). For weight-stable adults EER equals TEE. Recommended for all BMI categories (separate BMI equations showed no significant difference).
entries.nutripal_use: NutriPal's maintenance-energy estimate (tab 10, Step 2) and its eligibility rules (no estimate under 19).
entries.caution: Derived from US/Canadian doubly labelled water data; not validated on Malaysian adults.
entries.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2023

entries.guidance: Standard error of the predicted value: 241 kcal (women 19+) and 342 kcal (men 19+). About 68% of people with the same characteristics have a true requirement within +/-1 SE of the estimate, and 95% within +/-1.96 SE.
entries.nutripal_use: NutriPal shows the estimate as a range (EER +/- 1 SE, rounded to 10 kcal).
entries.caution: Present as an estimate, never as an exact requirement.
entries.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2023

entries.guidance: No valid, reliable tool exists to classify an individual's physical activity category; Table 7-1 gives example day patterns for inactive, low active, active and very active.
entries.nutripal_use: Basis for NutriPal's plain-language activity question (wording is a proposed implementation).
entries.caution: Tell users to pick the closest description; the category is approximate.
entries.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2023

entries.guidance: EER equations estimate energy for weight maintenance and do not predict the energy needed for weight change. An intake 1.96 SE below the EER would lead to weight loss in almost all people with those characteristics. Worked example: man, 45 y, 175 cm, 100 kg, low active, EER 3,041 kcal.
entries.nutripal_use: Why NutriPal uses the EER as a maintenance base for every limit and labels the goal change a general guide (R-EN-02).
entries.caution: Not a prescription; weight-loss targets are individualised by a clinician.
entries.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2023

entries.guidance: Consider reducing carbohydrate intake for some adults with diabetes; limiting processed foods is an effective way.
entries.nutripal_use: Supports showing carbohydrate per portion prominently.

entries.guidance: Emphasise minimally processed, high-fibre carbohydrate: at least 14 g fibre per 1,000 kcal.
entries.applies_to: People with or at risk of diabetes
entries.nutripal_use: Alternative fibre target scaled to the user's energy.

entries.guidance: Foods with at least 3 g fibre per serving are generally considered higher-fibre choices.
entries.nutripal_use: Per-serving positive insight that needs no daily target.

entries.guidance: Replace sugar-sweetened beverages, including juices, with water or low/no-calorie drinks; minimise foods with added sugar.
entries.applies_to: People with or at risk of diabetes
entries.nutripal_use: Drink-specific insight; added sugar can only be stated when the label lists it.
entries.caution: Do not infer added sugar from total sugars.

entries.guidance: Non-nutritive sweeteners can replace sugar-sweetened products in moderation and short term to cut calories and carbohydrate.
entries.applies_to: People with or at risk of diabetes
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Limit sodium to <2,300 mg/day as clinically appropriate, mainly by limiting processed foods.
entries.nutripal_use: Conflicts with Malaysian 2,000 mg; NutriPal keeps 2,000 mg (Malaysian priority).

entries.guidance: Limit foods high in saturated fat; follow general-population limits for saturated fat, cholesterol and trans fat; avoid trans fat; replace saturated fat with unsaturated fat, not refined carbohydrate.
entries.applies_to: People with or at risk of diabetes
entries.nutripal_use: Saturated fat can appear as a secondary insight for diabetes users.

entries.guidance: No evidence that protein above or below 0.8-1.5 g/kg/day (15-20% of energy) improves health; individualise. Do not go below 0.8 g/kg.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education; protein is shown, not judged.

entries.guidance: Include non-starchy vegetables, whole fruit, legumes, lean protein, whole grains, nuts, seeds, low-fat dairy; minimise red meat, sugar-sweetened beverages, sweets, refined grains and (ultra)processed foods.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: For overweight or obesity, aim for at least 5-7% weight loss.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education only.

entries.guidance: Do not exceed recommended daily limits; abstainers should not start; delayed hypoglycaemia risk, especially with insulin or secretagogues.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot safety note.

entries.guidance: Carbohydrate is the primary dietary determinant of post-meal glucose and guides prandial insulin; meal composition (fat, protein, fibre, alcohol) changes the response; low-carbohydrate patterns can be used with education and monitoring.
entries.nutripal_use: For T1D, carbohydrate is displayed as a count (g and 15 g exchanges) without a meal-budget verdict.

entries.guidance: Alcohol inhibits liver glucose output; hypoglycaemia risk lasts up to 24 h after the last drink.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot safety note.

entries.guidance: Refer to a prevention programme for at least 5-7% weight loss through a reduced-calorie eating pattern and >=150 min/week moderate activity; eating patterns such as Mediterranean or low-carbohydrate; no ideal macronutrient split.
entries.applies_to: Adults with overweight and high risk
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Weight loss of 5-15% is a primary target for many; 5-10% improves metabolism; 10-15% or more can lead to remission.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Weight loss of >=7-10% within 6 months is effective for prevention; encourage low-GI foods in the Malaysian context; >=150 min/week moderate activity.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education with Malaysian framing.

entries.guidance: Micronutrient, herb or spice supplements (e.g. chromium, magnesium, cinnamon) are not recommended for glycaemic benefit.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot: decline supplement advice.

entries.guidance: Lower sodium intake to <2,000 mg (5 g salt, 1 level teaspoon) per day.
entries.nutripal_use: Layer 2 daily sodium target.

entries.guidance: A diet with <2,000 mg sodium daily (5 g salt) can be beneficial to decrease CVD risk.
entries.nutripal_use: Confirms the same limit for all users.
entries.source: Ministry of Health Malaysia / Academy of Medicine Malaysia 2023

entries.guidance: Reduce sodium to <2 g/day (5 g salt) in adults (strong recommendation).
entries.nutripal_use: International confirmation.

entries.guidance: Reduce sodium to <2,300 mg/day, moving toward an ideal <1,500 mg/day. Sodium reduction may be contraindicated in severe symptomatic orthostatic hypotension.
entries.nutripal_use: Not the default; a 1,500 mg provider limit can be entered.

entries.guidance: Adopting the DASH eating pattern is recommended.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Increase dietary potassium from food in people with normal kidney function not at risk of hyperkalaemia; routine potassium, magnesium or calcium supplements are not supported.
entries.nutripal_use: Potassium on a label may be shown as information with a kidney/medication caution, never as a target.

entries.guidance: Dietary potassium 3,500-5,000 mg/day; except CKD or drugs that reduce potassium excretion (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, potassium-sparing diuretics, MRAs).
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education with exceptions.

entries.guidance: If using table salt, WHO suggests replacing it with lower-sodium salt substitutes containing potassium (conditional); adults only, not pregnancy or children, excluding kidney impairment.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education with exclusions.

entries.guidance: Potassium-based salt substitutes (25-30% KCl, 65-75% NaCl) can be useful, except with CKD or potassium-retaining drugs.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Losing 4-5 kg lowers systolic BP by 4-7 and diastolic by 3-6 mmHg in adults with overweight; aim for BMI 25 and waist 90 cm (men) / 80 cm (women).
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: People who drink should limit to 2 standard drinks/day (men) and 1 (women); 1 standard drink = 14 g alcohol. ACC/AHA: abstinence or <=1/<=2; 12-14 g per drink. Malaysian CPG: 10 g/20 g.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education; definitions of a drink differ (see conflicts).

entries.guidance: Regular green or black tea is recommended; the coffee-BP relationship is inconclusive.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Ingredient names that mean sodium include MSG, sodium benzoate, baking soda, disodium inosinate/guanylate, sodium phosphate, among others.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot only; ingredient lists are outside the nutrition table.

entries.guidance: Sodium per serving for common Malaysian foods, e.g. instant noodles 1,500 mg per 85 g packet; stock cube 2,208 mg per piece.
entries.nutripal_use: Familiar comparison anchors in explanations.

entries.guidance: Leave the gravy/soup, avoid adding salt or soy sauce, pick clear soup over cream soup, request less salt.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot tips.

entries.guidance: Sodium per 5 g: table salt 1,794 mg; bamboo 1,753; Himalayan pink 1,740; kosher 1,731; French sea salt 1,562. Potassium salt substitutes: 983-1,150 mg sodium per 5 g.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot: speciality salts are about as salty as table salt.

entries.guidance: Limit saturated fat to <10% of total energy.
entries.nutripal_use: Layer 2 saturated fat target.

entries.guidance: Replace saturated fat with polyunsaturated (and monounsaturated) fat; a diet rich in fruit, vegetables, nuts, legumes, whole grains and fibre lowers LDL-C.
entries.nutripal_use: Explains the swap advice in insights.

entries.guidance: Limit trans fat to <1% of total energy.
entries.nutripal_use: Layer 2 trans fat target.

entries.guidance: Trans fat in common Malaysian supermarket foods is generally very low (<1 mg/100 g).
entries.nutripal_use: Explains why trans fat is often 0 or missing.
entries.caution: Missing trans fat stays 'not listed', not zero.
entries.source: Ministry of Health Malaysia / Academy of Medicine Malaysia 2023

entries.guidance: Limit total fat to 30% or less of total energy.
entries.nutripal_use: Secondary nutrient for LDL; not a TG decider.

entries.guidance: Reducing dietary cholesterol to <200 mg/day should be considered; its link to blood cholesterol is weak and questionable. Limiting saturated fat lowers LDL more consistently than restricting dietary cholesterol.
entries.nutripal_use: Show cholesterol with context; never the deciding nutrient.

entries.guidance: Fibre 25-30 g/day (MDA); 20-30 g/day with 7-13 g soluble fibre (CPG); soluble fibre improves cholesterol and TG.
entries.nutripal_use: Total fibre is a benefit; soluble fibre cannot be inferred from total fibre.

entries.guidance: 2-3 g/day plant sterol/stanol from enriched foods is recommended.
entries.nutripal_use: Mention only if a label lists plant sterols.
entries.caution: Not a recommendation to buy supplements.

entries.guidance: Oat/barley beta-glucan >=3 g/day, soy protein >=25 g/day and 30 g mixed nuts/day are encouraged.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education; beta-glucan only if labelled.

entries.guidance: Adopting a Mediterranean diet is recommended for people with dyslipidaemia at increased CVD risk.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Weight loss improves lipids in overweight; MDA: BMI <25 and waist <90/<80 cm (B). Malaysian CPG: BMI <23 or 5-10% loss; waist <90/<80 cm.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot; cut-offs conflict (see conflicts).

entries.guidance: Saturated fat is typically in red meat, butter, high-fat milk, coconut, palm and palm kernel oil. SFA share of fat: coconut 91.9%, palm kernel 84.2%, palm oil 44.9%, palm olein 42.4%, olive 18.8%.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education for Malaysian oils.

entries.guidance: Unfiltered coffee raises LDL-C; filtered coffee does not; 3-4 cups/day probably not harmful.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: A diet low in added sugar, refined carbohydrates and saturated fat, minimising alcohol, is beneficial to reduce TG and ASCVD risk.
entries.nutripal_use: Defines TG deciders: sugars (proxy), saturated fat; fibre/whole grain as quality signal.
entries.caution: Only total sugars is usually on the label.

entries.guidance: 5-10% weight loss lowers TG by about 20%.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Replacing 1% of energy from carbohydrate with MUFA or PUFA lowers TG by about 1.7 and 2.3 mg/dL.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Reduce carbohydrate to 50-60% of energy with emphasis on whole grains; intakes above 60% raise TG.
entries.nutripal_use: Context for carbohydrate quality insight.

entries.guidance: Reduce refined carbohydrates and sweetened beverages; carbohydrate should be lower with high TG and low HDL.
entries.nutripal_use: Supports drink-sugar insight for TG.
entries.source: Ministry of Health Malaysia / Academy of Medicine Malaysia 2023

entries.guidance: For TG <5.6 mmol/L: restrict sugar-sweetened beverages; whole fruit over juice (3-4 servings/day); limit full-fat and sweetened dairy; total fat 30-35% of energy with saturated fat limited.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education; total fat is not a TG decider.

entries.guidance: Reducing alcohol with a diet low in refined carbohydrate (added sugar) and more activity can lower TG by 10-20%.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: With TG 1.7-11.3 mmol/L and cardio-kidney-metabolic features, referral to a dietitian can be beneficial.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot referral wording.

entries.guidance: Eating more energy than used leads to weight gain; less leads to loss; individual responses vary.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot: calories matter but responses differ.
entries.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2023

entries.guidance: To lose weight and keep it off, reduce calories from foods and drinks; metabolism slows during weight loss so needs fall.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Added sugars <10% of calories, saturated fat <10%, sodium <2,300 mg/day.
entries.nutripal_use: Supports the 10% free-sugar cap (US framing).

entries.guidance: Aim for at least 300 min/week of moderate activity to keep weight off; weigh regularly.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Start with losing 5-10% of starting weight over 6 months.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Read labels for calories, servings, fat, fibre, sodium and added sugars per serving; at restaurants eat about half and take the rest home.
entries.nutripal_use: Supports portion-aware insights.

entries.guidance: Aim to lose 0.5-1 kg a week; choose products with more green than amber or red traffic lights; swap sugary drinks for water; five 80 g portions of fruit and vegetables a day; 150 min activity a week.
entries.nutripal_use: Supports Layer 1 colours and the 500 kcal default (approx. 0.5 kg/week).

entries.guidance: Gain gradually with about 300-500 extra kcal/day; small frequent meals; add nuts, seeds, cheese, milky drinks; protein from beans, pulses, fish, eggs, lean meat; do not rely on chocolate, cakes and sugary drinks; see a GP for unexplained weight loss.
entries.nutripal_use: Source of the gain default (300 kcal more, lower end of the range; 500 as an option, R-EN-02); sugar and saturated fat still flagged.

entries.guidance: Monitor people pursuing weight loss for adequate protein and micronutrients.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot caution against crash diets.

entries.guidance: Dietary prescriptions should be individualised to motivation, age, sex, comorbidities, physical activity and weight-loss goals; medical nutrition therapy by a dietitian is recommended for overweight and obesity, especially with comorbidities.
entries.nutripal_use: Why NutriPal's goal change is a general, adjustable default, never a prescription (R-EN-02).
entries.source: Ministry of Health Malaysia, MEMS, MASO, MDA, FMSA 2023

entries.guidance: Calorie restriction should be individualised (age, sex, readiness, activity, comorbidities, preference). Any one of: 1,200-1,500 kcal/day for women; 1,500-1,800 kcal/day for men; or reduce daily energy by 500-750 kcal from usual intake, for an initial loss of 0.5-1 kg/week.
entries.nutripal_use: Source of the lose default (500 kcal less, lower end of the range) and the 1,200/1,500 kcal floors (R-EN-02); the full range is shown as education.
entries.source: Ministry of Health Malaysia, MEMS, MASO, MDA, FMSA 2023

entries.guidance: Up to 1 kg/week; up to 10% of baseline weight; 3-5% of baseline weight when cardiovascular risk factors are present (hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, hyperglycaemia).
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.
entries.source: Ministry of Health Malaysia, MEMS, MASO, MDA, FMSA 2023

entries.guidance: At least 150 min/week moderate activity has demonstrated weight maintenance; more than 300 min/week is associated with maintenance after weight loss.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.
entries.caution: Exercise clearance for people with obesity.
entries.source: Ministry of Health Malaysia, MEMS, MASO, MDA, FMSA 2023

entries.guidance: Calorie restriction should be combined with either low-carbohydrate or low-fat intake; meal replacement or intermittent fasting may be alternatives. Low-carbohydrate and balanced diets gave similar weight loss.
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot: no single diet is best for weight loss.
entries.source: Ministry of Health Malaysia, MEMS, MASO, MDA, FMSA 2023

entries.guidance: Programmes with high-frequency counselling (>=16 sessions in 6 months) targeting a 500-750 kcal/day deficit are recommended when available; if limited, alternative structured programmes (including remote or mobile app) may be considered. The deficit is about 1,200-1,500 kcal/day for most women and 1,500-1,800 for most men, adjusted for baseline weight.
entries.applies_to: Adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity
entries.nutripal_use: Context: deficits are set inside structured care, so NutriPal labels its goal change a general, adjustable guide (R-EN-02).

entries.guidance: Any magnitude of weight loss helps; 5-7% improves glycaemia and CV risk factors; sustained >10% gives greater benefits, including possible remission.
entries.applies_to: Adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot education.

entries.guidance: Individualise nutrition and keep general nutrition guidance while in deficit (8.9, A); very-low-calorie meals (800-1,000 kcal/day) only in medical settings (8.12, B); supplements not recommended for weight loss (8.13, A); monitor protein and micronutrient adequacy (8.14, E).
entries.applies_to: Adults with diabetes and overweight or obesity
entries.nutripal_use: Chatbot safety: no crash diets, no weight-loss supplements.

entries.guidance: EER predicts energy for maintaining current weight; to reach a desired weight, adjust intake and monitor weight.
entries.nutripal_use: Loss/gain adjustments are NutriPal design choices on top of EER.
entries.source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine 2023
